1.zh: 她一看到窃贼翻墙就立刻报警。
1.note: 感官动词 see 后接不带 to 的不定式 climb；应选（1）。

2.concept: 虚拟条件 — 与过去事实相反
2.zh: 若莉萨早知道玩具特卖，就会通知我们。
2.note: 与过去事实相反，从句用 had known；应选（4）。

3.concept: 主谓一致 — 主语为 collection
3.zh: 这批稀有钱币及若干古邮票正于展览中展出。
3.note: 主语 collection 为单数，动词用 is；应选（1）。

4.concept: 代词 — Each + 单数动词
4.zh: 每位宾客都领到一份欢迎礼包。
4.note: Each 作主语时动词用单数；应选（3）Each。

5.zh: 阿兹曼除了是出色钢琴家，也是熟练画家。
5.note: 表“除……之外还”用 Apart from；应选（1）。

6.zh: 李太太问：“她从很小就弹吉他，不是吗？”
6.note: 现在完成进行时，附加问句用 hasn't she；应选（2）。

7.concept: 主谓一致 — neither…nor 就近
7.zh: 拉欣和他的兄弟姐妹们每周四都与父亲打羽毛球。
7.note: 就近原则，siblings 为复数，动词用 enjoy；应选（1）。

8.concept: 固定搭配 — make a beeline for
8.zh: 那名坚定的登山者直奔山顶，想征服世界最高峰。
8.note: 习语 make a beeline for；应选（2）for。

9.zh: 她昨晚打来时，我已吃完晚饭。
9.note: 过去的过去用 had finished；应选（4）。

10.concept: 关系从句 — who 复数
10.zh: 路易斯是每年参加数学奥林匹克众多男生之一。
10.note: 定语从句 who 指 boys，动词用复数 participate；应选（1）。

11.stem_plain: The manager had to ___________ a plan to boost the sales of the company's products.

12.stem_plain: The pupils made an agreement to ___________ their differences and work together to complete their project.

13.stem_plain: Even after being caught cheating during the examination, William failed to ___________ the seriousness of the situation.

14.stem_plain: The teacher ___________ important information about the upcoming excursion to all her pupils.

11.zh: 经理必须制定计划以提升公司产品销量。

choices.eg: During morning assembly, our principal used invent in a sentence about teamwork and responsibility.
The manager had to devise a plan to boost the sales of the company's products.
In her composition, Mei Ling showed how the word concoct can change the tone of a paragraph.
The tour guide explained that visitors should remember the phrase fabricate when reading historical plaques.

12.zh: 学生们约定搁置分歧，合力完成项目。

choices.eg: The school had to put off the sports day because of the thunderstorm.
Please put down your pens once the invigilator says "time is up".
The pupils made an agreement to put aside their differences and work together to complete their project.
After the experiment, the science teacher asked us to use put away in a complete sentence of our own.

13.zh: 威廉考试作弊被抓后仍不明白事态严重。

choices.eg: In her composition, Mei Ling showed how the word seize can change the tone of a paragraph.
The tour guide explained that visitors should remember the phrase admit when reading historical plaques.
Even after being caught cheating during the examination, William failed to grasp the seriousness of the situation.
The coach reminded the players that grapple is common in sports commentary and news reports.

14.zh: 老师向全班广泛传达研学重要信息。

choices.eg: The tour guide explained that visitors should remember the phrase dispersed when reading historical plaques.
After the experiment, the science teacher asked us to use distributed in a complete sentence of our own.
The coach reminded the players that dispatched is common in sports commentary and news reports.
The teacher disseminated important information about the upcoming excursion to all her pupils.

15.zh: 官员警告地震迫在眉睫，随时可能袭来。

choices.eg: After the experiment, the science teacher asked us to use eminent in a complete sentence of our own.
The coach reminded the players that pertinent is common in sports commentary and news reports.
The government officials warned the residents of the city that an earthquake was imminent and could strike the area at any moment.
The reporter wrote that the rescue team had to act prominent before the storm grew worse.

16.note: 动词 guesses 意为无确凿证据的推测或瞎猜。在学术完形填空中，不及物动词 speculated 意为推测、猜测（常与 about/on 连用），是其最为对标的高级代换考点。
16.zh: 我们曾随意猜测病毒来源，一笑置之，直到疫情袭来。

choices.zh: 深思，仔细琢磨（作不及物动词，常与 over 连用）
choices.eg: The manager spent three days as he mulled over the business offer before making a final decision.
The committee carefully considered several options before upgrading the workshop operating procedures.
The independent supervisor questioned the laboratory results because the data looked inconsistent.
Medical experts across the globe speculated about the exact source of the mysterious new virus.

17.note: 形容词/副词短语 smashed 意为被无情地砸碎、摧毁。副词 ruthlessly 意为无情地、残忍地、极其猛烈地，在描写灾难或外部力量无情破坏的考点语境中最为契合。
17.zh: 经济像被拆迁球无情摧毁，冠状病毒后一片废墟。

choices.zh: 无情地，残忍地，极其猛烈地
choices.eg: The powerful category five storm hit the coastal local town ruthlessly, causing massive destruction.

choices.zh: 粗心地，马虎地，不小心地
choices.eg: He carelessly left his confidential files on the counter of the crowded primary school canteen.
The rescue engineering team proceeded cautiously into the badly damaged basement area.
The professional ice skater completed her complex dynamic routine effortlessly and won the gold medal.

18.concept: 近义词 — in the wake of（在……之后）
18.note: 介词短语 in the wake of 意为紧随某事之后发生、作为某事的后果（尤指不好的灾难性事件）。这与固定短语 in the aftermath of（在不好的事件或战争的余波/后果中）在学术辨析中互为精确近义词。
18.zh: 冠状病毒过后留下大面积破坏。

choices.eg: The researchers found themselves trapped in the midst of extreme chaos when the fire alarm rang.
Please use the nearest stone exit staircase immediately in the event of an unexpected building fire.

choices.zh: （语法不当/不符合常规英语习语固定搭配）
choices.eg: The assistant was reminded that using this specific phrasing in the composition was grammatically incorrect.

choices.zh: 在……之后（特指战争、灾难、疫情等产生的余波或严重后果中）
choices.eg: The local government launched a massive support plan in the aftermath of the severe winter flood.

19.note: 动词 rose 在形容病例、数据或数字在短时间内呈现明显的上升趋势时，不及物动词 climbed 意为攀升、爬升，是其直接替换的核心同义考点。
19.zh: 新加坡病例数升至六万例。

choices.zh: （数量/数字/价格等）攀升，爬升；爬，攀登
choices.eg: The total number of confirmed infection cases climbed sharply before the lockdown was enforced.

choices.zh: 提高（职位/层次），使升高（物理高度/情绪等，常作及物动词）
choices.eg: Regular morning exercise successfully elevated his overall mood and reduced his work stress.

choices.zh: 扩大，扩张，扩展（指体积、规模、范围或业务的变大）
choices.eg: The successful tech firm expanded its online business overseas to attract international buyers.

choices.zh: 上升，登高，攀登（多指正式语境下物理位置由低向高移动）
choices.eg: The travelers spent hours as they ascended the steep path toward the mountain top castle.

20.note: 名词 dismay 在固定搭配 Much to my dismay 中意为“令我沮丧/失望的是”。在修饰事态发展未达预期并让人失落的语境下，直接对标固定结构 Much to my disappointment（令我失望的是）。
20.zh: 令我失望的是，病情似乎每小时都在加重。

choices.zh: 恐惧，惊恐（用于 Much to my horror 意为令我惊恐的是）
choices.eg: Much to my horror, the old wooden bridge collapsed into the river during the sudden storm.
The engineer sighed in frustration when the computer program crashed for the third time.
She managed to hide her annoyance despite being constantly interrupted by her talkative teammate.

choices.zh: 失望，扫兴（用于 Much to my disappointment 意为令我失望的是）
choices.eg: Much to my disappointment, our school soccer team lost the final championship match yesterday.

cloze: It all started as a small influenza in China. We thought we were safe. We thought it was nothing serious – a small virus could not cause much trouble, could it? We made [Q16 (guesses)] about its origin, laughing about it as we went, until it hit us.

It came harder than anything we had faced. The virus claimed lives by the thousands. Our economy was [Q17 (smashed)] like a wrecking ball, leaving nothing but mass destruction [Q18 (in the wake of)] the coronavirus. We thought it was all over.

In Singapore, the number of cases [Q19 (rose)] to 60 000. It was 14 January 2020. That week, I went to work as usual despite not being in the pink of health. However, to my [Q20 (dismay)], my condition seemed to worsen with each passing hour. Heat pulsated through my body, almost knocking me down. Popping a mint, I boarded a taxi to the nearest clinic, hoping for the best.
zh: 一切始于中国的一场小流感。我们以为安全，以为不足为惧——小小病毒能掀起多大风浪？我们随意猜测来源，一路说笑，直到疫情真正袭来。
打击空前猛烈，病毒夺走成千上万生命。经济像被拆迁球无情摧毁，冠状病毒过后满目疮痍。我们一度以为一切都完了。
新加坡病例升至六万，那是2020年1月14日。那周我身体不适仍去上班，却失望地发现病情每小时加重，浑身发烫几乎站不稳，含一片薄荷糖搭出租车去诊所，只求好运。

21.stem_plain: What should be the top priority when planning an outdoor adventure?

22.stem_plain: Why is the colon (:) used in **'How to assemble a survival kit:'**?

options.1: to emphasise the importance of a survival kit
options.2: to list the steps on how to assemble a survival kit
options.3: to simplify facts and information about a survival kit
options.4: to give more information about the survival kit in a specific order

23.stem_plain: Which of the following item is not one of the basic recommended items found in the survival kit?

24.stem_plain: Which of the following is true about the survival kit?

options.1: It should not be shared among family and friends.
options.2: It should not be filled to the brim with items.
options.3: It should be able to fit in one's pocket.
options.4: It should only include the basic items.

25.stem_plain: What is the focus of Camp Leap's activities?

options.1: encouraging solo exploration to discover hidden wonders
options.2: providing thrilling experiences for children of all ages
options.4: offering a serene environment for relaxation

26.stem_plain: In **'This outdoor adventure camp will cater for up to 100 participants this year – the largest number thus far'**, the dash is used here to __________.

options.2: highlight the total number of participants
options.3: emphasise that the information is important
options.4: indicate that the information is the main idea

27.stem_plain: Mrs Raja wants to register her child for Camp Leap. What must she do?

options.4: register in person at Sunny Forest Campsite

28.stem_plain: What is the main purpose of the article?

options.1: to attract readers to attend Camp Leap
options.2: to encourage readers to go on outdoor adventures
options.3: to recommend possible school holiday activities to the readers
options.4: to remind readers on important safety tips for outdoor adventures

21.note: Article states safety is the number one priority and advises pack wisely before setting off → (4) packing the necessary items. Fun and nature (1)(2) are secondary.

22.note: After How to assemble a survival kit: the colon introduces the numbered steps that follow → (2).

23.note: Basic steps list strip + matches, pencil, tubes, plasters, foil — not keeping a whole matchbox with matches as a separate basic item (3). Pencil (1), foil (2), straws (4) appear in the steps.

24.note: Text stresses a pocket-sized container you can carry → kit should fit in one's pocket (3).

25.concept: 细节 — Camp Leap 主旨
25.note: Camp Leap blurb highlights teamwork and lifelong friendships (3), not solo exploration (1) or mere relaxation (4).

26.note: The dash after 100 participants this year adds extra information (the largest number thus far) → (1).

27.note: Flyer: visit www.teamleap.sg to register and pay online → (1). Email is for enquiries (3); in-person venue (4) is not required.

28.note: Article teaches outdoor safety tips and survival-kit packing; Camp Leap ad reminds readers to bring a kit — overall purpose (4) remind readers on important safety tips. (1) is secondary for the camp flyer half.

cloze: Travellers acquainted with Singapore will probably already know of our city's national icon — the mythical Merlion. There are seven authorised Merlion statues [Q29] the island, the most well-known [Q30] the one found at Merlion Park, a popular Singapore landmark.

Before you visit this tourist spot, you may want to learn more about the symbolism [Q31] the Merlion, and how it intertwines [Q32] our nation's history. According to legend, Sang Nila Utama, a prince, landed on our shores amidst a storm. He spotted a strange creature which he identified as a lion. He saw this [Q33] a good omen and decided to name the island "Singapura", [Q34] means Lion City in Sanskrit.

Today, the Merlion continues to be a beloved symbol of Singapore. You can glimpse echoes of this legend, embodied [Q35] the statue at Merlion Park. Spouting water [Q36] its mouth, the Merlion statue stands [Q37] 8.6 metres and weighs 70 tonnes. Originally located at the mouth of the Singapore River, it was built by Lim Nang Seng, designed by Kwan Sai Kheong, and unveiled on 15 September 1972 by then Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

[Q38] completion of Esplanade Bridge in 1997, the statue could no longer be viewed clearly from the waterfront and was relocated to the Merlion Park. As you travel around Singapore, try to spot other statues of our city's national icon!
zh: 熟悉新加坡的旅客多半知道国鱼鱼尾狮。全岛有七座官方鱼尾狮雕像，最著名的在鱼尾狮公园。
参观前可了解鱼尾狮的象征意义及其与国家历史的交织。传说室利·尼罗·乌塔玛王子风暴中登陆，见奇兽认作狮子，视为吉兆，将岛命名为梵语'狮城'Singapura。
今日鱼尾狮仍是新加坡深受喜爱的象征；公园雕像体现这段传说，狮口喷水，高8.6米、重70吨，1972年由李光耀总理揭幕。
1997年滨海桥建成后从海滨望不清，雕像迁至鱼尾狮公园。游览时请留意其他鱼尾狮雕像。

29.note: statues across the island = spread throughout Singapore. 故填'A — across'。

30.note: the most well-known being the one at Merlion Park — appositive naming the famous statue. 故填'H — being'。

31.note: symbolism behind the Merlion = the meaning underlying the icon. 故填'G — behind'。

32.note: intertwines with our nation's history. 故填'Q — with'。

33.note: saw this as a good omen. 故填'C — as'。

34.note: Singapura, which means Lion City — non-defining relative clause. 故填'P — which'。

36.note: Spouting water from its mouth. 故填'J — from'。

38.note: Upon completion of Esplanade Bridge = after it was completed. 故填'M — upon'。

cloze: Being adventurous, Tom decided to explore the dense woods. After hiking for an hour, he stumbled upon a [Q39(hiding)] cave. Excited by the prospect of discovering something new, Tom entered the cave. He [Q40(maneuvered)] his way along the winding pathway. Little did he [Q41(knew)] of the danger that was awaiting him. As he [Q42(vanchered)] deeper into the cave, he soon found himself stuck in a narrow passageway.

Tom tried to wriggle his way free, but the rocks around him were too [Q43(tight)] packed. With heartbeat racing and [Q44(panicked)] rising within him, he started screaming for help. Filled with [Q45(dispare)] , Tom was about to give up hope. Then, he [Q46(rimambered)] something his grandfather had told him — there was always a way out if one stayed vigilant. With a renewed [Q47(cence)] of determination, Tom began to scour the walls of the cave, [Q48(searched)] for any crack or opening. [Q49(When)] looking for two hours, he finally found a hole big enough for him to squeeze through. Tom pushed through the hole and finally [Q50(emreged)] into the light. A wave of relief washed over him as he took in a deep breath of fresh air.
zh: 爱冒险的汤姆决定探索密林。徒步一小时后他发现一处隐蔽洞穴，兴奋入内，沿蜿蜒通道小心前进，却不知危险在等待；他越往深处钻，不久便卡在狭窄通道里。
他扭动脱身但岩石挤得太紧；心跳加速、恐慌涌起，他大喊求救，几乎绝望。忽然想起祖父的话：保持警觉总有出路。他重燃决心搜刮洞壁，两小时后发现可钻过的缝隙，终于见到天日，深吸一口新鲜空气，如释重负。

39.note: hiding cave → adjective hidden (a cave that was hidden).

41.note: Little did he know — inverted structure takes base verb, not knew.

43.note: Rocks were tightly packed — adverb modifies packed, not adjective tight.

44.note: panicked rising → noun phrase panic rising within him.

48.note: began to scour … searching for — parallel participle, not past searched alone.

49.note: After looking for two hours — not When looking.

cloze: Do you know that 8 February is National Kite Flying Day? It is a day to encourage people to get out and enjoy the process of making a kite and flying it. On this day, kite enthusiasts mark the day by [Q51] together to showcase their individual kites and flying them. While the exact origin of kite-flying is unknown, it is believed to have originated in China thousands of years ago. It has since gained [Q52] as a recreational activity all over the world, bringing joy and excitement to people of all ages and walks of [Q53].

The first kite was [Q54] of simple materials like wood and cloth. Gradually, kite designers have experimented with new materials and designs have evolved [Q55] the years, with modern kites made from nylon fabric which is tear resistant, lightweight and durable. In the early years, kites were often made to [Q56] the shape of birds. Today, they come in elaborate and unique designs. Some kites even have LED lights attached [Q57] them to allow for night flights and fun light shows.

Kite [Q58] are organised in many countries where enthusiasts come together to showcase their creativity. These competitions are a delight to spectators, as they witness the sky decorated with colourful kites that can [Q59] intricate tricks.

Kite-flying offers [Q60] than just entertainment. You can learn important [Q61] through the experience of kite-flying. For example, patience is required as you [Q62] for the wind to pick up and carry the kites. Perseverance is also needed when a kite fails to launch immediately. Launching the kite in the air may require some running. You can exercise while having fun and may not even realise how [Q63] exercise you have done. [Q64] you finally get your kite up, the thrill of seeing something in motion and tossed about by the wind can be a truly uplifting [Q65]. So, if you want to get out and about with a novel activity with your family, try kite-flying!
zh: 2月8日是全国放风筝日，鼓励人们制作并放飞风筝。爱好者相聚展示作品；风筝源于中国，现已成为全球受欢迎的休闲活动，为各年龄层带来欢乐。
最早的风筝由木布等简单材料制成；设计随年月演进，现代多用耐撕裂的尼龙。早期常做成鸟形，如今造型各异，有的还装 LED 便于夜飞。
各国举办风筝比赛，观众欣赏空中彩色风筝表演惊险特技。
放风筝不止娱乐：可学耐心等候风起、失败重试的毅力，奔跑放线也锻炼身体；风筝升空随风舞动是振奋的体验——不妨全家一试。

51.note: 介词 by 后面需要接动名词。与后面的 together 组合，指放风筝爱好者通过“聚在一起”或“集会”来庆祝这个日子，故填入动名词 coming / gathering / meeting。

52.note: 作为动词 gained 的核心宾语。指放风筝作为一项娱乐活动在全世界“赢得了名气”或“变得流行”，完美契合高频书面短语 gain popularity / traction。

53.note: 属于各类英语考卷中极其高频、核心的固定经典习语 walks of life，意为吸引着来自“各行各业/不同背景”的男女老少。

54.note: 前面有助动词 was，后面紧跟介词 of。完美契合表示原料构成的经典特定短语 be made of，表示第一只风筝是由木头和布料等简单材料“制成”的。

55.note: 表示“这些年来”或“随着时间的推移”。over the years 是最为地道的高频固定时间介词短语，而 throughout the years 在语意上也通顺。

56.note: 不定式符号 to 后接动词原形。指早期的风筝经常被制成用以“类似于”、“模仿”或“像”鸟类的形状，填入动词原形 resemble / mimic / match / copy（若填 look 需与后文的 like 组合，此处原句为 the shape，填入 resemble 最佳）。

57.concept: 过去分词与介词特定搭配
57.note: 与前面的过去分词 attached 完美组合。指有些风筝甚至把LED灯“安装”、“连接”或“固定”在上面，构成专属搭配 attach onto/to/on them。

58.note: 修饰名词主语。根据后面的复数谓语动词 are organised 以及后文的 These competitions（这些比赛），说明许多国家都会组织风筝“比赛”或“节庆”，故填复数名词 competitions / festivals / tournaments。

59.concept: 情态动词后的动词原形
59.note: 情态动词 can 后面接动词原形。与后面的名词 tricks（特技/花招）组合，指风筝能够在空中“表演”或“做出”复杂的特技动作，完美契合专属动宾短语 perform tricks 或者是 do tricks。

60.note: 后接比较连词 than just entertainment。完美契合固定数量结构 offers more than...，表示放风筝所带来的好处“不仅仅是”娱乐和消遣。

61.note: 修饰名词宾语。后文具体列举了 patience（耐心）和 perseverance（毅力），说明通过放风筝你可以学到很多重要的“品质”、“美德”或“课程”，故填复数名词 values / virtues / lessons / qualities。

62.note: 在 as 引导的原因从句中，主语为 you，后面紧跟介词短语 for the wind to pick up。完美契合高频核心搭配 wait for someone/something to do something，表示当你“等待”风力变强时，需要付出耐心。

63.concept: 程度限定词与不可数名词搭配

paragraphs.1: 十二岁的本眼神明亮，他不知所措地站在林先生面前。“林先生，我很难理解。您是建议我把鸽子送回我发现它的地方吗？”
paragraphs.4: 林先生轻声叹息，疲惫地点了点头。“的确，我正是这个意思，”他回答道，声音中透着一丝精疲力竭。与此同时，在同理心和忧虑的驱使下，本继续恳求道。“但是林先生，”他哀求着，语气中带着诚挚，“它受伤了。难道我们不应该对弱者表现出同理心吗？”
paragraphs.8: 就在那时，在本怀抱的纸箱里安身的鸽子动了动，它拍打着未受伤的翅膀，发出轻柔的咕咕声。林先生冷淡地看了一眼，目光沉思地停留了片刻，随后又将注意力转回到本身上。他接着回应了这个小男孩想要救助这只受伤鸟儿的真诚愿望。
paragraphs.12: “我理解你高尚的意图，而且我必须承认，对动物有这样的同理心确实值得赞扬，”林先生开口道，语气中带着真诚。“然而，实话实说，对于这个可怜的生物，我们无能为力。如果我们有时间，可以把它送到防止虐待动物协会（SPCA）。但即便我们能做到，他们所能做的也只是将其安乐死。”听到这话，本盯着林先生，惊讶地瞪大了双眼。
paragraphs.16: “但是，林先生，”他充满乐观地插话道，“断掉的翅膀肯定很容易治好。难道 SPCA 不能提供必要的护理吗？”
paragraphs.19: “你到底知不知道这个世界上有多少计其数的鸽子？”林先生问道，声音中带着一丝隐约的烦躁。本措手不及，只是耸耸肩作为回应，他意识到不能再靠耸肩来表达自己的不确定了。他鼓起勇气回答道：“也许有一百万只？”
paragraphs.23: “把那个数字乘以四百倍，”林先生反驳道，他的话语中掩饰不住不耐烦。本困惑地望着老师。然而，林先生脸上刻画出的表情显示他打算传达一个重要的观点。
paragraphs.26: “那相当于惊人的四亿只鸽子，”林先生澄清道，语气中带着紧迫感。“我还有……”他停顿了一下，目光移向手表，“……七分三十一秒就要去上课了。因此，我不可能把这只鸽子——四亿只中的仅仅一只——送到 SPCA，只为了让他们不可避免地结束它的生命。我猜你休息时间结束后也有课吧？”
paragraphs.31: “是玛丽老师的英语课。但我可以翘课，回头再补上。我们今天只学诗歌，”本说。“那根本不是重点。你我都没有奢侈的时间。想一想四亿只鸽子与我们共存的现实吧。少了一只会产生很大的区别吗？把鸽子送回原处。到那时，正好是你上英语课的时间。好吗？”
paragraphs.36: “但是林先生……”察觉到本的坚持，林先生立刻挥了挥手打断，本的话语悬在半空。不等本说完，林先生就转身回了教职员室。本的心沉了下去。在别无选择的情况下，他照着林先生的吩咐做了。
paragraphs.40: 那天与林先生的谈话产生的内疚感一直萦绕在本的心头，直至今日。随着他渐渐长大并开启了教育工作者的生涯，这成了一个他会反复分享的故事，用以强调林先生当年未能教会他的道理。本希望在学生心中种下一种深刻的美德，那是多年前他在与林先生的接触中所缺失的。他会问学生一个一直沉重地压在他良心上的问题：“如果纸箱里的是你，会怎样呢？”

  2. (b) 行 38：Ben's heart sank — 失望、沮丧。

  2. (b) that（行 23）：指 Ben 猜的 a million 鸽子数量。
  3. (c) it（行 31）：指 English lesson with Mrs Marie。

answer.79a: Ben's plan to save the wounded pigeon

80.note:
1. (a) 行 45：让学生设身处地想象自己在纸箱里，体会鸽子处境。
  2. (b) 教导对弱者无论情形如何都要同理心（empathy） — 林先生当年未教的美德。

answer.80a: Ben wanted his pupils to put themselves in the shoes of the pigeon.
answer.80b: Ben was trying to teach his pupils to show empathy to the vulnerable no matter what.
